When the crap hit the fan in the Technology subreddit, I feel part of the reason for all the anger was that the admins had never set forth a plan as to what happens when the users of a subreddit essentially "revolt", throwing it into an unusable state. With no set plan, users kept going for a while in the hopes that the admins might actually do something, since this was a very rare, if not the first time, occurrence. While Whoaverse isn't large enough to need a plan right now, setting one forth early on will at least make sure users don't go overboard in the hopes that something might happen when there is no plan.

This will be difficult to implement in a way that makes everyone happy, and I'm not sure that it will even ever be used, but I feel this is something that Reddit got wrong that cost them big time for trust. That's something we can learn from and improve upon. Schools have fire, bomb, tornado, etc drills for a reason: To be prepared if a situation goes horribly wrong. I think we need a plan so that, if and when the shit hits the fan, we've got some umbrellas.
I feel there needs to be a plan for what happens when a large or default subverse gets into massive crap.
Meh. I worry any such plan could be abused. Just upvotes. Let users do as they wish, even if they riot.

Honestly, I keep finding massive flaws in every plan I think of. If the admins added themselves as top mods on a subverse, they'd have to act as moderators and admins. If the moderators could get removed, how would it be determined that they do and who they're replaced by?

That's part of the reason I want to get the idea out there as soon as possible: so we have a lot more time to think about it.

What are the plans you've thought of? I'd be interesting in reading about them.

We already have this and this in terms of ideas for an elected moderator system.

I propose that we have some general principles or thumb rules that should not be violated by a subverse's activity. If they are violated, top admins of whoaverse itself become authorized to step in and clear the mess in that sub verse. Sample rules:

1) Number of active mods to total members in a sub verse should have a limit ratio (say 1:100 or 1:1000 or whatever).

2) At least one site admin should be a moderator of verses of particularly large size, say 100,000 members or so.

Note that these limits could be set and changed by the Atko or by the site admin themselves. But it would be preferable to have these values trransparent and have them grow big as whoaverse gets big.
